surfaces.part: top cap (white band with diamond mark over teal band)

answer.evidence: The cap width profile runs 9, 13, then 15 for rows 3-8, then drops straight to 9 at row 9. It is rounded only at the top corners and has a flat bottom edge sitting on the narrower shaft, so it is a hat or flat band cap, not an ellipse plate. The white rows 2-4 and teal rows 5-7 look like a front-facing banded strip. There is no distinct front-edge line and no eave shadow, so no clear horizontal top surface. The shaft (rows 9-26, with the yellow number panel on rows 11-21) and the flared base (rows 27-30) are drawn only as vertical faces with no top. This matches the 'column: flat band cap' reference, which is marked wrong.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style exit sign: a gray post with a light cap and a dark-teal number panel showing a '2'. It reads at the same scale as the references. Measured facts: 13 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12) and below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, with no 5x5 flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted, a dark teal/blue-gray tone like the references, and not a sticker-style black line. Shading is about 4 steps on the post (highlight, light, mid, dark), a bit shallower than the 5-6 on the richer references, but it matches the shipped modern_city pieces. The post carries modest texture and the sign is crisp. A careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking thinner or flatter.
